subject.title: Matrix DM session-key lowercasing collides case-distinct MXIDs, sharing one peer's DM transcript with another under per-peer scope

question: Should the security fix preserve only Matrix direct MXID case now, or also enroll Signal direct peers in the same case-preserving registry change?
rationale: The Matrix source path and DM isolation contract are clear, but broadening the shared registry to Signal direct changes another channel's session-key boundary without the same direct-ID contract proof in this review.

options.title: Fix Matrix direct first
options.body: Preserve Matrix direct peer case under non-main DM scopes now, with legacy-row safeguards, and leave Signal direct unchanged until separately proven.

options.title: Enroll Matrix and Signal direct
options.body: Preserve both Matrix and Signal direct IDs in one registry change, but require direct-ID contract proof and regression tests for both channels before merge.

options.title: Wait for live homeserver proof
options.body: Defer implementation until a permissive or legacy Matrix homeserver demonstrates the full inbound-to-transcript leak, trading speed for stronger runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Fix Matrix direct first
recommendation.body: Preserve Matrix direct peer case under non-main DM scopes now, with legacy-row safeguards, and leave Signal direct unchanged until separately proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent discussion and co-authored fixups on the same Matrix session-key alias/migration safety area make this the strongest routing candidate for the security-boundary decision.
